initialization: Both arms start with 16 exact copies of the balanced joint-retention final model and evolution seed 1. One paired exploratory search, not a multi-seed estimate. The first two evaluated populations must have identical genomes and numeric scores.
scoring: Both arms first protect the same 616 demonstrated successes (157 precision and 459 matches, including the focal pair), then maximize recovery of the five remaining original matches. Completion fields and all episode formulas are identical. Broad uses the previous precision/whole-match progress priorities, with remaining-case scores appended only to resolve complete ties. Focused moves those two remaining-case progress terms ahead of broad progress. The five frozen cases, not a changing failure subset, contribute remaining progress; terrain variants retain equal episode weight.
control_scope: Both arms add the same strict current-success protection gate. Broad is the broad-progress control under that gate, not an exact replay of the preceding total-count recipe.
selection: Save the first winner passing all 621 cases, if any, and each final winner at generation 48. Freeze identities before post-training evaluation. No observation or excluded-case result selects a model or changes the budget.
post_training: Reevaluate the common seed, original reference, first-full artifacts if present and final artifacts on all 157 precision cases and 482 match states. Ten other additional cases and eight diagnostics stay outside breeding. No fresh worlds in this comparison.
interpretation: Controlled change in progress priority while protecting the same current successes. All cases and the starting model are known development data. Full known-case success is required before separately frozen fresh qualification. Network, inputs, action decoding, physics, host gates and production behavior do not change.
